newsitem.title: USA: Transitional Hospitals accepts Vencor offer.
newsitem.headline: Transitional Hospitals accepts Vencor offer.

text.p: Transitional Hospitals Corp. on Thursday accepted a $639 million cash takeover offer from Vencor Inc. following a six-week fight for control of the health care company.
In accepting Vencor's bid of $16 per share, Las Vegas-based Transitional called off a $582 million merger pact struck last month with privately held Select Medical Corp.

"Even though we had not expected our aggressive growth plans for THC to be interrupted via a sale of the company, our board of directors believed that this transaction with Vencor is in the best interests of Transitional's shareholders," Transitional Chief Executive Officer Richard Conte said in a news release.

Louisville, Ky.-based Vencor launched an offer for Transitional on May 7, just two days after Transitional had agreed to be bought by Select Medical for $14.55 per share. Transitional, formerly called Community Psychiatric Centres, then agreed to enter talks with Vencor.

Transitional operates 16 long-term acute care hospitals and three satellite facilities in 13 states. It also owns a 61 percent interest in Behavioural Healthcare Corp., which provides psychiatric and behavioural health services based in Nashville, Tenn.

The combined company will have 58 hospitals, 314 skilled nursing centres, more than 4,000 institutional customers for contract ancillary services, more than 80,000 employees and pro forma annual revenues of about $3.3 billion.

In a statement issued jointly with Vencor on Thursday, Transitional said its board had recommended that shareholders accept Vencor's $16-per-share bid. Vencor's tender offer was scheduled to expire midnight on June 19.
Select Medical, based in Mechanicsburg, Pa., could not be reached for comment.

The move is the latest in a wave of consolidation sweeping the industry that provides hospital and nursing care. Earlier this week, long-term health care company Genesis Health Ventures Inc. announced it was teaming with two private investors to buy Muticare Cos. Inc. for $1.4 billion.

"The addition of Transitional expands our network of long-term acute care hospitals that provide the foundation for our health care continuum. Together, we can offer payors and patients a full spectrum of high-quality outcomes-oriented, cost-efficient healthcare services," said Vencor Chairman Bruce Lunsford.
Vencor was not available to comment on the transaction's impact on earnings or anticipated cost savings from the deal.
Vencor stock rose $1.375 to $43.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Transitional stock was unchanged at $16, also on NYSE.
